reviews.text: With Pain and Glory, Almadovar may have made his best film since Talk to Her.
reviews.author: Calum Cooper

reviews.text: Pain and Glory is the year’s most powerful depiction of reconciliation, and a commentary on the art of moviemaking as a portrait of one’s soul, all summarized in what may be the best final shot of the entire year.
reviews.author: Brendan Cassidy

reviews.text: Many meta films can be so insightful to a creator’s life, but this might be one of the most beautiful films in the sub-genre.
reviews.author: Ryan McQuade

reviews.text: Pain and Glory, oscillates between constant antagonisms that cross the protagonist's feelings and function dialectically: Eros and Thanatos. The entire story expose the view of Salvador (Almodóvar's alter-ego) about his past.
reviews.author: Denise Pieniazek

reviews.text: In addition to the stellar performances and sumptuous cinematography, Pain and Glory is a compassionate and realistic portrait of the bittersweet realities inseparable from a life near completion.
reviews.author: Paul Kanieski

reviews.text: The number one movie of the year was undoubtedly the magnificent Pain and Glory (Dolor y Gloria).
reviews.author: Brian T. Carney

reviews.text: Antonio Banderas in Pain & Glory gives a stunning, career-defining performance.
reviews.author: M.N. Miller

reviews.text: Pedro Almodovar finds a perfect and surprising match in Antonio Banderas.
reviews.author: Jane Freebury

reviews.text: …essential for the director’s fans, but perhaps a little dry and self-absorbed for the general public...
reviews.author: Eddie Harrison

reviews.text: Far removed from the restlessly stylistic mode of his earlier work, Pain and Glory shows the filmmaker exercising patience and dimension, resulting in a feature that emphasizes the essential place of cinema in his life.
reviews.author: Brian Eggert

reviews.text: It is beautifully and richly textured.
reviews.author: Lonita Cook

reviews.text: If it looks and sounds cinematic, Almódovar shows an uncharacteristic level of restraint in his storytelling. For fans of the director, this will come as a satisfying treat, but is likely to leave newcomers to his cannon somewhat cold.
reviews.author: Ben Turner

reviews.text: Stripped of Almodóvar's signature kitsch aesthetic and larger-than-life narratives, the film becomes a powerful confessional tale on the nature of storytelling.
reviews.author: Yasmin Omar

reviews.text: Exteandia's Alberto steals the spotlight from Banderas' Salvador. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Gustavo Herrera Taboada

reviews.text: A career-best performance from Antonio Banderas. Pedro Almodóvar provides us with a complex emotional story of personal growth and exploration​.
reviews.author: Bianca Garner

reviews.text: Without his noted frivolity and transgressiveness, how much is there to Almodóvar's work? Entire stretches of Pain and Glory are terribly dull, flat and mundane.
reviews.author: David Walsh

reviews.text: "The film may seem to start as a film filled with regret and looking at your past but instead finishes within an incredible sense of optimism"
reviews.author: Shaun Alexander

reviews.text: Pain and Glory is Pedro Almodovar looking back at his own storied career, one full of personal choices, refusals, and decisions that defined who he is.
reviews.author: Dan Buffa

reviews.text: Antonio Banderas... is tremendously layered as the despondent Salvador.
reviews.author: Matthew St. Clair

reviews.text: The most autobiographic of Almodovar's films, not only because of the story but also of the cast [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Gisela Savdie

reviews.text: Almodóvar's ability to be both ultra-contemporary in his settings and ultra-modern in describing the past are unique in the cinema.
reviews.author: A.S. Hamrah

reviews.text: Glory came accompanied by pain, feels absurd but, isn't reality absurd? An impecable work from both Banderas and Almodovar. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Victor Pineyro

reviews.text: There's no denying the potency of the performance at its centre, with Banderas delivering what is potentially a career-best masterclass.
reviews.author: Tom Beasley

reviews.text: Pain and Glory is the Spanish auteur's scrapbook of memories culled from his own life -- a fictionalised self-portrait which journeys into the heart, mind and soul of a man mesmerised by movies and weakened by numerous maladies.
reviews.author: Prahlad Srihari

reviews.text: Has the aesthetics that always characterize his style and some moments of affectivity, but it lacks emotional strength and I immediately perceive that it becomes self-indulgent with the story of the film director. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Yasser Medina

reviews.text: It's sometimes funny and mostly pretty grim, but the patient pacing and wistful dialogue give even the bleakest moments a sense of bittersweet beauty.
reviews.author: Alex Hudson

reviews.text: Pain and Glory not only shows a brilliant artist still operating at the peak of his creative powers, but also reunites him with his most important male lead.
reviews.author: David Lamble

reviews.text: Pain and Glory is a patient film, it quietly sits in wait, encouraging you to create new memories by revisiting your own old memories.
reviews.author: Andrew F. Peirce

reviews.text: Banderas is the best part of the movie, with a tour-de-force performance...a master filmmaker forging a new path...
reviews.author: Shawn Edwards

reviews.text: We are seeing the world - in all its sadness and beauty - through his eyes. Banderas brings it all to life.
reviews.author: Catherine Capellaro

reviews.text: As slow and meandering as the film feels at times, DP José Luis Alcaine's eye is a constant that enlivens the screen when the narrative struggles to.
reviews.author: Steven Sheehan

reviews.text: In his assemblage of the film, Almodóvar imbues "Pain & Glory" with a wonderfully lyrical lilt. He weaves the film's many themes gracefully, with the measured contemplation of a musician putting together an album.
reviews.author: Derek Deskins

reviews.text: Like many of Almodovar's films, this one is emotional and personal. I think this film appeals to an older audience with its story about reconnecting with one's emotional center, after suffering despair brought on by age and medical problems.
reviews.author: Robert Roten

reviews.text: Courtesy of Almodóvar's masterful direction and a career-finest performance from Banderas, we feel every moment with Salvador. The pain, the glory, and everything in-between.
reviews.author: Charlotte Harrison

reviews.text: I love seeing Banderas directed by Almodóvar, especially in this role which is obviously a stand-in for the director himself. He uneasily occupies the screen, clearly trying to manage both his pain and his loved ones' response to it.
reviews.author: Jas Keimig

reviews.text: This certainly feels like we know much more about the film's creator than from any of his (Almodóvar) other films.
reviews.author: Katie Hogan

reviews.text: Tonally, this is nothing new for Almodóvar, but there's something truly special about the groove he finds with Banderas.
reviews.author: Jonah Koslofsky

reviews.text: From his time in the wilderness, Almodóvar has emerged with a stunner. Heavily introspective, Pain and Glory is about aging and finding a reason to go on when your body fails and inspiration is lacking.
reviews.author: Jorge Ignacio Castillo

reviews.text: Its strands of fictionalized memoir work decently, but it's its more insightful look at religion and art throughout childhood that bring something to the table.
reviews.author: Matt Cipolla

reviews.text: Pedro Almodóvar's latest film is a masterpiece that balances the personal with the relatable.
reviews.author: Mina Takla

reviews.text: Almodóvar fills this late-career masterwork with all his obsessions... But he layers them with the contemplation and melancholy of an older artist reflecting on his life, without sentimentality but with soulfulness.
reviews.author: Loren King

reviews.text: Banderas ... is consistently good at conveying vulnerability, but he takes it to another level here, delivering a performance that captures the exhaustion and frustration of a full life.
reviews.author: Cameron Meier

reviews.text: Pain and Glory finds (Antonio) Banderas working with (Pedro) Almodóvar for an 8th time, and the two are magic together.
reviews.author: Michael Ward

reviews.text: While still embracing the visual facades that make his films such a pleasure to watch, Pain and Glory finds him stripping away the emotional facades, bringing us closer to him than ever before.
reviews.author: Kathleen Sachs

reviews.text: Banderas has never been more tender-and beautiful.
reviews.author: Marlow Stern

reviews.text: We hadn't seen an Almodovar so lucid and passionate for so long... Pain and Glory is affectionately crafted with courage and intimacy
reviews.author: Filipe Freitas

reviews.text: A curiously uninvolving effort from Pedro Almodovar...
reviews.author: David Nusair

reviews.text: It's laden with Almodóvar's typical penchant for soapy melodrama, but it remains grounded thanks largely to the finely tuned work of lead actor Antonio Banderas.
reviews.author: Mike Scott

reviews.text: It's a genre that is often self-indulgent - and occasionally angry and aggrieved - but in the hands of the 70-year-old Spanish master becomes a gentle and generous examination of time, age and the act of creation.
reviews.author: Alison Gillmor

reviews.text: A deeply personal film, like Pedro Almodóvar was letting him into his personal diary. Such a powerful piece of cinema
reviews.author: EJ Moreno

reviews.text: Banderas' performance is so towering, so finely shaded yet thrillingly unvarnished, that the film feels at many a moment ready to burst with all the raw feeling bottled up inside it.
reviews.author: Isaac Feldberg

reviews.text: Pain and Glory is like getting a letter from Almodovar, but what's here is not all in words. He may not quite be the last filmmaker left who understands the power of color, but his eye has little equal; he notices the harmony of colors.
reviews.author: Richard von Busack

reviews.text: Far from Almodóvar's masterpiece, but there couldn't be a finer capstone to his career than this reckoning with what that career has brought him to.
reviews.author: Tim Brayton

reviews.text: The cast and the direction, particularly the shifting moods, make the film worth several viewings.
reviews.author: Damien Straker

reviews.text: Almodóvar pleads allegory and the question the film asks, and the filmmaker-within-the-film unwittingly asks, is: how does one maintain or rediscover not only desire, but also first desire? The spark. The fire. The riveting earliest impulses and insights.
reviews.author: Ray Pride

reviews.text: There is jubilation and wonder to be found in these remembrances, moments of pure bliss that are beyond imagining.
reviews.author: Sara Michelle Fetters

reviews.text: Both emotionally dextrous and finely paced.
reviews.author: George Elkind

reviews.text: It is [Pedro] Almodovar in a minor key, and it takes some getting used to.
reviews.author: Philip Martin

reviews.text: Salvador knows he has to stop making mistakes and find the key to a rebirth of his many passions - filmmaking, love, friendships. Much of what Banderas is called upon to do is act from an interior point-of-view. He does so brilliantly.
reviews.author: Michael Calleri

reviews.text: A film about aging and retrospection, it's a series of solid scenes that don't build to much; not a lot "stays with you." But one of its saving graces is that you get the sense Almodóvar might be OK with that.
reviews.author: Margot Harrison

reviews.text: Perhaps this movie's greatest accomplishment is reminding us what a great actor Banderas is.
reviews.author: Kristian M. Lin

reviews.text: [Pain and Glory] stands out from the rest of the filmmaker's filmography. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Ruben Peralta Rigaud

reviews.text: Anchored by strong work from Antonio Banderas, this is a quiet, reflective piece of work that simmers with emotion.
reviews.author: Micheal Compton

reviews.text: Though few could possibly relate to it all, Almodovar's smart, meaningful and moving sprinkling of observations and memories actually should leave at least a little something for anyone to embrace.
reviews.author: John Urbancich

reviews.text: No matter how close this story is to Almodóvar's own truth, he makes this story feel real, which maybe is all that matters.
reviews.author: Sean P. Means

reviews.text: The latest from Pedro Almodóvar is quiet and introspective as his latest autobiographical stand-in explores a late-in-life rut.
reviews.author: Christopher Lloyd

reviews.text: After too long a fallow period, Pedro Almodóvar has returned to form, or even improved on it, with Pain and Glory, the most candidly autobiographical film he's ever ventured.
reviews.author: Stuart Klawans

reviews.text: Almodóvar never experienced a creative dry spell like the one depicted here, but after a couple of relatively ho-hum efforts in I'm So Excited! and Julieta, Pain and Glory feels like the work of a new man.
reviews.author: Daniel Barnes

reviews.text: Banderas earns his best actor prize from Frances' Cannes Film Festival -- and seems to be a shoo-in for an Oscar nod -- with his magnetic turn as Salvador Mallo, celebrated filmmaker plagued with a cavalcade of physical maladies.
reviews.author: Brandy McDonnell

reviews.text: Almost feels like an exorcism, an autumnal reverie filled with pain and regret, of mistakes made and loves lost. And yet there's a glimmer of hope as Almodóvar wrestles with his demons through the medium he loves.
reviews.author: Mattie Lucas

reviews.text: Almodovar makes this internal trip a spellbinding and soulful exercise - whatever other things he has in common with his avatar here, being creatively blocked isn't one of them.
reviews.author: Rob Thomas

reviews.text: As an emotional narrative it is a spectacularly engaging work, an evocation of one man's life so rich and moving that it burrows deep and will not be dislodged.
reviews.author: Robert W. Butler

reviews.text: There's plenty going on here and much of it is tantalisingly murky and unsaid, and yet this is still an affectingly human drama featuring gorgeously restrained playing from Antonio, Penélope [and] Nora Navas...
reviews.author: David 'Mad Dog' Bradley

reviews.text: The nostalgia here is predominantly of the self-critical kind, and that makes a world of difference.
reviews.author: Rubén Rosario

reviews.text: In classic Almodóvar fashion, Pain and Glory is suffused with a deep love of all kinds of art .
reviews.author: Nadine Smith

reviews.text: In his Hollywood career, Banderas tapped his manic energy. All that gets bottled in here, as Salvador tends to watch and reflect, an artist observing everything around him, saving everything for future use.
reviews.author: Robert Horton

reviews.text: Pain and Glory considers both elements of its title, and though the former weighs heavy, it's the warmth that lingers - in the small moments that resonate in life's absurd slipstream...
reviews.author: Luke Goodsell

reviews.text: Pain and Glory might be the most sublime work either of the men has had their name on for many years.
reviews.author: Graeme Tuckett

reviews.text: [Antonio] Banderas' remarkably nuanced performance does plenty of this film's heavy-lifting and elevates it into something quite sublime.
reviews.author: Toby Woollaston

reviews.text: Almodóvar shows us that, even after nearly two dozen features over several decades, he can still hold an audience in his hand - and surprise it.
reviews.author: Moira MacDonald

reviews.text: Moving, beautiful and, ultimately, an ode to the power of art.
reviews.author: Laura DeMarco

reviews.text: A masterful, melancholy, tender, lacerating self-examination, filled with colour and light and the ghosts of those he has loved. Almodovar at 70, and perhaps astonishing to himself, continues to grow.
reviews.author: Paul Byrnes

reviews.text: Pain & Glory is a beautifully realized picture in a remarkable body of work that continues to inspire.
reviews.author: Kiko Martinez

reviews.text: Director Pedro Almodóvar has poured himself into an intimate, unflashy, semi-autobiographical accounting of the ageing process.
reviews.author: Andiee Paviour

reviews.text: Salvador says he writes to excise pieces of himself too difficult to face when it actually renders him vulnerable enough to revisit and embrace the fondness [that remains].
reviews.author: Jared Mobarak

reviews.text: For all those cinemagoers who have been enthralled by Almodovar's work over the years this very personal movie, with its superbly pitched central performance by Banderas, will be immensely rewarding.
reviews.author: David Stratton

reviews.text: Antonio Banderas is riveting in Pedro Almodóvar's pensive, nostalgic, and contemplative Pain and Glory.
reviews.author: Roxana Hadadi

reviews.text: Almodóvar takes what could be cathartic only for himself and shares it with all of us.
reviews.author: Jonathan W. Hickman

reviews.text: A two hour exercise in navel gazing. However Antonio Banderas gets better and better with age as an actor.
reviews.author: Jackie K. Cooper

reviews.text: Slowly, what feels like a series of disconnected vignettes set over the course of a lifetime shapes up into something resembling a throughline.
reviews.author: John Lui

reviews.text: What's most impressive here is the quietly amusing way Banderas conveys both the agony and ecstasy of his situation.
reviews.author: Ken Eisner

reviews.text: There is much emotional nakedness in front of and behind the camera, and the wistfulness stays with you long after the credits roll.
reviews.author: Jeanmarie Tan

reviews.text: A lugubrious piece about an ageing man who, if not exactly undergoing a full-on epiphany, makes marginal, elegiac steps towards a more hopeful future.
reviews.author: PJ Nabarro

reviews.text: It's a testament to the restraint and sheer evocative beauty of [Pedro Almodóvar's] writing that the film never resorts to cheap, sensationalistic plot devices.
reviews.author: Zhuo-Ning Su

reviews.text: Hardcore Almodóvar fans will swoon at the metatextural layers herein, but more casual cineastes, fans of excellent cinema wherever it can be found, will also marvel at the control over tone, pacing, palette and emotion...
reviews.author: Joe Gross

reviews.text: Structured, sublimely stylized conclusion to his trilogy, cinematically summarizing Pedro Almodovar's life and work.
reviews.author: Susan Granger

reviews.text: Pain and Glory is a impressive bit of cinema but it is, more importantly, a rich film experience for thoughtful audiences, both warm, bittersweet and satisfying.
reviews.author: Cate Marquis

reviews.text: Pain and Glory does not quite reach the heights of Almodóvar's best works. However, there is still plenty to enjoy here.
reviews.author: Courtney Small

reviews.text: As always with Almodóvar's films, the art direction vibrantly expresses the environment for each scene, with credit to Maria Clara Notari's expressive design.
reviews.author: Diane Carson

reviews.text: ...it's a great director looking inward, matched with an actor giving it all he's got and going to places we never knew he was capable of.
reviews.author: Tom Santilli

reviews.text: Almodovar, as always, is in fine form, but Banderas's performance makes the movie.
reviews.author: Robert Denerstein

reviews.text: ...a film that's all about making sense of the present by coming to terms with the past.
reviews.author: Sarah Boslaugh

reviews.text: In Pain and Glory, Almodovar brings together fiction and biography to create a knotty self-portrait...[It is] the latest chapter in what has become an autobiography of anxieties and obsessions.
reviews.author: Ben Flanagan

reviews.text: As you might expect, it leads to a touch of self-indulgence, as the movie equips its straight-forward plot with some deliberate pacing, but it also provides a potent and emotional experience.
reviews.author: Eric Eisenberg

reviews.text: Antonio Banderas gives his best, most committed performance in years as a film director looking back over his life in "Pain and Glory," a typically rich, layered film from director Pedro Almodóvar.
reviews.author: Adam Graham

reviews.text: The end result is a work that is both one of the best movies of the year and sure to be considered one of the high-water marks of Almodovar's entire career.
reviews.author: Peter Sobczynski

reviews.text: ...one of Almodovar's least exuberant productions - and one of his best.
reviews.author: Josh Larsen

reviews.text: Banderas creates a shadow image of Almodóvar, with similar hair and physique, without becoming a replica. It's a very controlled performance.
reviews.author: Marjorie Baumgarten

reviews.text: Just as Mallo does in the film's final moments, Almodóvar reaches into the past to find new ways to create, to evolve, and eventually, find glory from pain.
reviews.author: Hayden Cornmell

reviews.text: [Banderas'] work is exquisitely in sync with what Almodóvar is attempting to achieve, painting for us a soul aching to be released.
reviews.author: Chris Feil

reviews.text: It's a mellifluous, touching story right up to the final shot, a clever reveal that brings the past and the present back together.
reviews.author: Chris Knight

reviews.text: This is a less purposefully provocative Almodovar film, evocative and understatedly emotional, acted with a mature grace by Banderas.
reviews.author: Jim Slotek

reviews.text: A triumph for Banderas. It's the kind of performance that makes you feel like you're seeing a familiar face for the first time.
reviews.author: Sean Burns

reviews.text: Almodóvar captures the intimate feeling of having your wounds and memories repaired by time.
reviews.author: Siddhant Adlakha

reviews.text: There's no shortage of films about struggling artists, and Almodovar's film beautifully epitomizes the concept.
reviews.author: James Clay

reviews.text: "Pain & Glory" is so awash in magnificence it's hard to decide who to praise more: its filmmaker, Pedro Almódovar; or its mesmerizing star, Antonio Banderas.
reviews.author: Al Alexander

reviews.text: Almodovar crafts another achingly beautiful effort that's mindful of human fallibility.
reviews.author: Brian Orndorf

reviews.text: Almodóvar gets personal in Pain and Glory, his best film since 2009's Broken Embraces.
reviews.author: Jeff Mitchell

reviews.text: As I admired Banderas' performance, and both the film's striking beauty and its soul-baring honesty, I almost that ennui too oppressive.
reviews.author: Max Weiss

reviews.text: There's plenty of artfulness on display in the intertwining of life and what gets made of it, but also a fair helping of artifice. Art imitating life, but also improving it a bit.
reviews.author: Matthew Lickona

reviews.text: Penelope Cruz as Salvador's mother... [is] in a contained and delicious performance. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Laura Hiros

reviews.text: "Pain and Glory" stays with you, and grows richer with reflection.
reviews.author: Randy Cordova

reviews.text: Almodóvar pulls off a nice trick with this movie, moving his protagonist and us from despair to a new lease on life with an ease that feels magical.
reviews.author: David Harris

reviews.text: It's one more example here of Almodóvar's ability to take pairs - not just people, but concepts (like, say, present and past, or pain and glory) - and happily join them.
reviews.author: Mark Feeney

reviews.text: Pain and Glory quite rightly asks its audience to appreciate Almodóvar while he's still mining his soul for melodrama every few years.
reviews.author: Chance Solem-Pfeifer

reviews.text: Almodovar masterfully handles flashbacks, making past and present seem naturally connected. He shifts from truth to fiction with deftness and clarity. He inspires viewers to question the reliability of memory.
reviews.author: Anita Katz

reviews.text: "Pain and Glory" generates tremendous emotion as it unfolds. This is an exceptional film by a mature director who taps into his own pain in ways that create great art. His efforts are buoyed by Banderas's fantastic performance which captures that magic.
reviews.author: Gary M. Kramer

reviews.text: Despite its sometimes-grim subject matter, "Pain and Glory" has plenty of Almodóvar's playful humor and love of the absurd.
reviews.author: Chris Hewitt

reviews.text: A sublime dance between the past and present ensues. Banderas' performance becomes the constant in the center, fluctuating between mournful disappointment and the nervous anticipation for artistic rebirth.
reviews.author: Glenn Heath Jr.

reviews.text: Autobiographical? Apparently. Stay with it, it's worth it.
reviews.author: Kelly Vance

reviews.text: [Antonio] Banderas, so soulful and integral to the film, gives the performance of his career and should be rewarded for it come awards season.
reviews.author: Tom Meek

reviews.text: The quiet, deliberate and slowly building "Pain & Glory" may not have all the exuberant cinematic flourishes for which Almodóvar is known but its power rests in its restraint.
reviews.author: Cary Darling

reviews.text: The well-crafted movie offers many expressive moments for the grateful director to look back on.
reviews.author: Dennis Schwartz

reviews.text: The script, penned by Almodóvar, doesn't go deep enough to be considered either a great character study nor strong situational drama. While this is a laudable minor film worth seeing, in a pantheon of many great projects and at least two masterpieces...
reviews.author: Paula Farmer

reviews.text: Everything, notably the interiors, are simply too beautiful to be anything but the work of an exalted imagination.
reviews.author: John Anderson

reviews.text: [Antonio] Banderas saves the day and is a revelation as his mentor's alter-ego. His nuanced performance fills in the cracks of this moderately engaging and slightly indulgent self-portrait.
reviews.author: Dwight Brown

reviews.text: One of the best pictures of 2019. Antonio Banderas, Asier Etxeandia, and Leonardo Sbaraglia that shine brightest in Almodóvar's 21st full-length feature.
reviews.author: Joe Friar

reviews.text: Emotions and eye-popping colors tell the director's deeply personal story, with Antonio Banderas front and center.
reviews.author: Richard Roeper

reviews.text: Pain and Glory is Almodóvar's best work in years, because it sings its message rather than shouts it.
reviews.author: Julie Crawford

reviews.text: The final shot of Pedro Almodóvar's achingly beautiful Pain and Glory is the stuff that cinematic perfection is made of.
reviews.author: Lisa Trifone

reviews.text: An intensely personal work, a painful, yet somehow serene exposing of Almodóvar's innermost thoughts and fears.
reviews.author: Jeffrey M. Anderson

reviews.text: It's the storytelling, never rushed, nuanced and complex, weaving bits of animation and design effortlessly throughout, that resonates the most.
reviews.author: Jeff York

reviews.text: The disconnected memories and disparate gripes of Almodóvar's protagonist never quite cohere into a compelling whole, though the colors are nice.
reviews.author: Vincent Mancini

reviews.text: The sort of exquisite, quietly observed film that gets its audience to lean forward.
reviews.author: Alan Zilberman

reviews.text: Art imitates art imitating life in Pedro Almodóvar's brilliant, autobiographical new film.
reviews.author: André Hereford

reviews.text: The movie's expressive moments-and there are many-are largely uprooted, decontextualized, and dematerialized, planted like index cards rather than allowed to unfold and to develop.
reviews.author: Richard Brody

reviews.text: However authentic Pain and Glory may be to Almodóvar's life, the film itself is bracingly, nakedly authentic in its emotional truth.
reviews.author: Mark Dujsik

reviews.text: We may not emerge from the film transformed, but we have at least been visually regaled.
reviews.author: Christopher Llewellyn Reed

reviews.text: The filmmaker contemplating his own creation as a man and an artist...plays as a poetic remembrance of things past, a reconciliation of self, powerfully capturing the emotional essence of keenly formative experiences and deep loves.
reviews.author: Peter Canavese

reviews.text: What remains so seductive about Almodovar is the way he replicates the movement of thought, creating a seamless weave between the story moving forward - rather minimal in this case - and the richer, more luminous past.
reviews.author: Erica Abeel

reviews.text: Pain and Glory is a celebration of art, not just as a form of entertainment or provocation, but as lifeblood.
reviews.author: Alex Leininger

reviews.text: Almódovar delights in our weirdness and our everyday hurts, while showing us how wondrous they can be. All these things are more true and more solemn in 'Pain and Glory' than I have ever seen them.
reviews.author: Sherin Nicole

reviews.text: Pedro Almodovar's cinematic masterpiece gives Antonio Banderas his career best performance shot in vivid color, haunting score. A definitive must-see!!
reviews.author: Carla Renata

reviews.text: Pain and Glory, Almodóvar's superb new film, scintillates with the same empathy and auto-fictional flair of earlier works, but opens up a new chapter where the two can come together.
reviews.author: Leonardo Goi

reviews.text: The most emotionally naked feature [Pedro Almodovar] has delivered yet.
reviews.author: Peter Gray

reviews.text: I like it... [But] I did feel like there was some pulled punches here. Perhaps because [the film] is too personal.
reviews.author: Wade Major

reviews.text: "Pain and Glory," all about healing rifts and rejoining life, is personal and universal. It's also simple in a way that's incandescent - suffused by a strange and beautiful gentleness of spirit.
reviews.author: Mick LaSalle

reviews.text: Almodóvar strips down his aesthetic to its barest bones and explores his themes with a calm demeanor that contrasts with the high melodrama that many observers associate with his career.
reviews.author: Juan Barquin

reviews.text: Along with his trademark visual flourishes, Almodovar finds dark humor to balance the off-putting nature of Salvador's behavior. As usual, Banderas and Cruz are up for the filmmaker's challenge.
reviews.author: Todd Jorgenson

reviews.text: Pain & Glory made me feel even more than I thought I would, opening the floodgates for a classic New York subway cryfest.
reviews.author: Jourdain Searles

reviews.text: Almodovar's given us a film that's got a soft surface but a hard, distinguished core at its center. He hasn't changed; he's adjusted. He's mellowed out - and he's more than earned it.
reviews.author: K. Austin Collins

reviews.text: A fun and tightly crafted autofiction that confronts the realities of aging in an entertaining, honest light.
reviews.author: Rendy Jones

reviews.text: The colors alone will inspire doctoral dissertations.
reviews.author: Bob Mondello

reviews.text: Antonio Banderas gives a career-best performance in Pedro Almodovar's most personal film yet.
reviews.author: Pete Hammond

reviews.text: Warm, tender and profound. It's one of the best films of Almodóvar's career. Antonio Banderas gives an Oscar-worthy performance.
reviews.author: Avi Offer

reviews.text: This isn't the first time writer/director Pedro Almodóvar has gone the autobiographical route in his filmmaking, but this may be the most moving, his 22nd full length theatrical feature carefully considered, deeply felt and vulnerably revealing.
reviews.author: Laura Clifford

reviews.text: The gifted writer-director strikes a Fellini-esque pose as he takes us on this journey through his life, intermingling memories both happy and poignant. Ultimately I must throw off any misgivings that remain and bow to a true master
reviews.author: Leonard Maltin

reviews.text: Pain and Glory is at once the gentlest and most emotionally naked movie Pedro Almodóvar has ever made.
reviews.author: Bilge Ebiri

reviews.text: A nostalgic summing up and a bold aesthetic breakthrough that brings the past to vibrant life.
reviews.author: Tim Appelo

reviews.text: Painful for sure, but glorious too, Pain and Glory is Spanish wunderkind Pedro Almodóvar's best and most moving film in years-a brave and wrenching self-portrait of an aging artist under the siege of age and the fear of death.
reviews.author: Rex Reed

reviews.text: All these performances (Pain and Glory is the best-acted film of year) idealize complicated human relations.
reviews.author: Armond White

reviews.text: Here [Pedro] Almodovar isn't focusing on generating suspense, he does something more special and that is he truly shares and not just entertains.
reviews.author: Alci Rengifo

reviews.text: There is something thrilling, not dulled, in the very honesty of the film, and in the vigor with which feelings, expressed at any age, can strike us like a slap in the face.
reviews.author: Anthony Lane

reviews.text: In a way, casting Banderas is yet another special piece of Almodóvar's biography he's added into this highly personal film. Just don't take the film literally.
reviews.author: Johnny Oleksinski

reviews.text: In looking back together, us and him, we cherish the beautiful memories and enduring bond that Salvador and Federico have. We have it with Almodovar and his movies.
reviews.author: Murtada Elfadl

reviews.text: Pedro Almodovar, with "Pain and Glory," brings us into his life and presents all the baggage he carried, both physically and emotionally, through that life and long career.
reviews.author: Robin Clifford

reviews.text: Performing at his mature finest, Banderas moves up and down the emotional register from mournful to puckish to regretful to freshly hopeful with a restraint that dials down Almodovar's breathy melodrama almost to straight realism.
reviews.author: Ella Taylor

reviews.text: Mixes darkness with light, melancholia with drollery, nostalgia with renewal, and regret for lost love with ineffable tenderness.
reviews.author: Joe Morgenstern

reviews.text: Antonio Banderas has never been better than he is here. The connection he has with Almodovar is clear, moving, and utterly effective.
reviews.author: Joey Magidson

reviews.text: "Pain and Glory" can be achingly sad, but its pleasures, rainbow hues and humor keep it (and you) aloft.
reviews.author: Manohla Dargis

reviews.text: A surprise in all ways except its surpassing quality, "Pain and Glory" reveals master Spanish director Pedro Almodóvar forging dazzling new paths while being completely himself.
reviews.author: Kenneth Turan

reviews.text: Some may find the film too loosely plotted, a series of vignettes more than a single, tight narrative. But they only need to sit back, listen to the beautiful score by Alberto Iglesias, and let Almodovar weave it all together.
reviews.author: Jocelyn Noveck

reviews.text: Even as he's gotten older, Almodóvar puts in enough here to suggest he has a ways to go before stopping.
reviews.author: Aaron Neuwirth

reviews.text: This thesis on creation is Almodóvar's best and most essential film in years.
reviews.author: Nathanael Hood

reviews.text: A beautifully crafted self-portrait from Alomodóvar, elevated by Antonio Banderas' affecting performance. A rich dose of intimate cinema, with an addictive nostalgia flavor. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Nestor Bentancor

reviews.text: Pain and Glory is a great director's rumination on the act of making art in itself - what stops an artist from working, and how to rediscover the glory of filmmaking.
reviews.author: Lauren Humphries-Brooks

reviews.text: Mature semi-autobiographical tale best for Almodovar fans.
reviews.author: Jennifer Green

reviews.text: Banderas helps make the journey look rougher than it is.
reviews.author: Mike D'Angelo

reviews.text: Another beautiful and brilliant piece of art and storytelling from Almodovar and a welcome return to form both for him and for Banderas.
reviews.author: Edward Douglas

reviews.text: Working with the legends of his long career to operationalize his past, Almodovar crafts a singularly unique and medium-specific autobiography in which cinema is inextricably linked to his own story, to his heart, soul and body.
reviews.author: Katie Walsh

reviews.text: Antonio Banderas gives the performance of his career playing Pedro Almodovar, the director who discovered him. 'Pain and Glory,' suffused with memory and regret, is one of Almodovar's greatest films and a moving tribute to both their talents.
reviews.author: Peter Travers

reviews.text: It doesn't all work, but by and large, this is a thoughtful, and often quite funny, retrospective on the artist and their struggle to create.
reviews.author: Matthew Dougherty

reviews.text: As an intricate study of reflection and regret, companionship and bliss, Pain and Glory is simply stunning.
reviews.author: Jazz Tangcay

reviews.text: When he's good, he's really good! Almodóvar's most personal is also one of his most profound. The more personal Pain and Glory gets, the more powerful it becomes for the viewer.
reviews.author: Dustin Chase

reviews.text: A scene never rings false in Pain and Glory, even when they're particularly humorous or ridiculous. If anything, that quirky quality is what makes each moment work.
reviews.author: Karl Delossantos

reviews.text: A well done, thinly disguised biopic of Pedro Almodovar's life
reviews.author: Harvey S. Karten

reviews.text: This is definitely a comment rather than a question, but the fictional film director's Q&A in Almodvar's delicious movie is the most glorious I've ever seen.
reviews.author: Sarah Cartland

reviews.text: Pain is probably too small, too sad, and too obtuse to really recommend as any kind of starting point. For longtime fans, though, it's a gift; the kind of quiet glory worth waiting a few decades for.
reviews.author: Leah Greenblatt

reviews.text: The profound melancholy that suffuses the film results from two artists contending with their senescence, with their prolific careers and their attendant triumphs and misfires.
reviews.author: Melissa Anderson

reviews.text: An advanced-career masterpiece of self-reflection.
reviews.author: Jon Dieringer

reviews.text: Above all, the third installment of the Spanish director's semi-autobiographical trilogy is a love letter to cinema.
reviews.author: Monique Vigneault

reviews.text: This is perhaps the director's most outstanding work since his peerless fin-de-siècle diptych of Talk to Her and All About My Mother.
reviews.author: Ed Frankl

reviews.text: Emotional and sensitive, Pain and Glory works like an intimate embrace, one that stings and soothes all at once.
reviews.author: Oliver Whitney

reviews.text: Pedro Almodóvar's latest is an intensely personal and sensuous return to form.
reviews.author: Meg Shields

reviews.text: Antonio Banderas offers a nuanced and moving performance in Almodóvar's most personal and introspective film. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Rene Sanchez

reviews.text: A lovely, tender work of art that finds beauty in personal pain.
reviews.author: Chris Evangelista

reviews.text: Pain and Glory is a film to savour like a fine bourbon, watching how Salvador (and Almodóvar) wrestles with demons of the mind, heart and body.
reviews.author: Peter Howell

reviews.text: Banderas, who won Best Actor at Cannes and deserves further recognition, has never been so bold, wily, and vulnerable.
reviews.author: Pat Mullen

reviews.text: Pain and Glory is a gem.
reviews.author: Bill Chambers

reviews.text: We get melodrama, comedy, infographics and theatrical monologues, all moving toward a sensuous climactic sequence that beautifully illustrates that how things happen can be more cinematically exhilarating than why they happen.
reviews.author: Kevin Ritchie

reviews.text: It's as touching, uncompromising and arousing as anything Almodóvar has made, even if it is a departure.
reviews.author: David Bax

reviews.text: Alive with the rich greens, blues, oranges and yellows of Almodovar's incomparable colour palette
reviews.author: Jay Stone

reviews.text: A deeply personal and very moving film, anchored by the best work of Antonio Banderas' career.
reviews.author: Brian Tallerico

reviews.text: Asier Etxeandia occasionally threatens to steal the show with his delicious turn as an exuberant addict, but perhaps the bravest thing here is Banderas' reserved performance.
reviews.author: Kate Taylor

reviews.text: Antonio Banderas is compelling in Almodovar's best work of late, full of the physical pain of life and the spiritual glory of film-making, in this deeply personal and at times heart-breaking tale
reviews.author: J. Don Birnam

reviews.text: A rebirth for both actor and director, Pain and Glory sees Banderas and Almodóvar at the peak of their electric, heart-wrenching capabilities.
reviews.author: Luke Parker

reviews.text: With Pain and Glory Almodóvar and Banderas remind us just how magical and enduring their professional relationship - past and, we can only hope, future - has been.
reviews.author: Alexandra Heller-Nicholas

reviews.text: Pain and Glory is perceptive about how artists double-down on their aesthetic peccadillos and subject matter in their late periods-audiences be damned-and tender about how bodily wear eventually snakes its way into every artist's signature.
reviews.author: Angelo Muredda

reviews.text: Banderas offers the greatest performance of his career, and Almodóvar's beautifully poignant ending is a rebirth for both actor and director.
reviews.author: Robert Daniels

reviews.text: The film is beautiful to look at, emotionally and intellectually engaging and extraordinarily soulful.
reviews.author: Anne Brodie

reviews.text: Antonio Banderas delivers a stand-out performance as filmmaker Salvador Mallo in Pain and Glory...
reviews.author: Danielle Solzman

reviews.text: Pain and Glory is a tapestry, stitching together timelines and characters, all towards a whole that you weren't quite expecting, but once it's thrown over you, the effect is one of Almodovar's warmest and most enjoyable films yet.
reviews.author: Matt Rodgers

reviews.text: It's a film that both redefines and rejuvenates the careers of both the director and star, while reminding viewers just how formidable [they] can be.
reviews.author: Andrew Parker

reviews.text: Pain and Glory is a compelling film which makes us sympathise with a complex, sensitive human being, his loves, friendships and regrets. He is someone who missed so much of life, yet created so much.
reviews.author: Alexa Dalby

reviews.text: As a portrait, "Pain and Glory" is less a mirror than an impressionistic painting. It's an emotional rendering of a person, not a literal one.
reviews.author: Michael O'Sullivan

reviews.text: It's the director's most moving film in years.
reviews.author: Amy Taubin

reviews.text: An ideal leisurely movie for a late-summer evening.
reviews.author: Edward Porter

reviews.text: A quiet, quirky delight that treads softly, often beautifully, between melancholy and joy.
reviews.author: Alison Rowat

reviews.text: The film will appeal to longtime fans of his, but it also stands alone as a memoir of a poverty-stricken, sun-drenched Catholic childhood, reflected upon by a man whose powers are waning.
reviews.author: Kate Muir

reviews.text: It's the filmmaker not just reassessing his own legacy, but acting as the curator of his legend.
reviews.author: Kevin Wight

reviews.text: It all adds up to a richly satisfying work from a film-maker whose love of cinema, in all its pain and glory, shines through every frame.
reviews.author: Mark Kermode

reviews.text: All this customary excellence is in the service of a story that, though drenched in the sourness of mortality, allows in cautious optimism about the human condition.
reviews.author: Donald Clarke

reviews.text: It's an exquisitely put together film, beautifully designed, much of which has lingered in my memory, but I wonder how much interest and pleasure someone unfamiliar with Almodóvar's previous work could derive from it.
reviews.author: Nick James

reviews.text: Pain and Glory is anchored in a terrific performance by Banderas: minimal gestures and economical conversations give little away. As such, the mysteries of the past unfold delicately over the course of the film.
reviews.author: Maria M. Delgado

reviews.text: Movingly elegiac.
reviews.author: Paul Whitington

reviews.text: While we're never quite sure how much is direct autobiography, the result is revealing, hugely emotive and arguably his most mature work to date.
reviews.author: Trevor Johnston

reviews.text: Nevertheless, the final shot - which justifies Penélope Cruz's seemingly incongruous casting - delivers the sort of elegant rug-pull that reminds us why Almodóvar is as revered as he is.
reviews.author: Alistair Harkness

reviews.text: Pain and Glory, is wonderfully restrained and all the better for it
reviews.author: Deborah Ross

reviews.text: [Antonio] Banderas has a tentative charm - he is always holding something in reserve - and is captivating in an encounter with an old flame, Federico, but he's fighting a losing battle against the lugubriousness of the material.
reviews.author: Ryan Gilbey

reviews.text: Almodóvar is the master craftsman here, but ultimately, the film is carried high on Banderas' shoulders. Even if you already know him outside of his more comic Hollywood work, he's on stunning dramatic form here as the frazzled artist.
reviews.author: Mark Harrison

reviews.text: About as Almodóvar as Almodóvar gets. It is also, undoubtedly, one of the director's best works and among the best films of the year.
reviews.author: Christopher Machell

reviews.text: Pain and Glory wants to be 8 1/2 but seemed to me about six-and-a-quarter.
reviews.author: Nigel Andrews

reviews.text: This auteur on the verge of a nervous breakdown is his masterfully understated summation of how it feels to outlive your notoriety, health and maybe times, and still make art from the memories.
reviews.author: Nick Hasted

reviews.text: Call it suspense then, but it's of a very sophisticated kind. Superb.
reviews.author: Paddy Kehoe

reviews.text: It marks Almodóvar at a height of cinematic mastery, with a film that is beauty at its finest and most pure.
reviews.author: Ben Rolph

reviews.text: Antonio Banderas shines in the role of a lifetime. His ability to capture the essence of Almodovar down to the most inconsequential detail, makes it seem as though he was born to play this very role.
reviews.author: Linda Marric

reviews.text: Forget Quentin Tarantino's Once Upon A Time In Hollywood, this is what a true love letter to cinema looks like.
reviews.author: Larushka Ivan-Zadeh

reviews.text: Pain and Glory is a karmic triumph, using memory and chance to champion the idea that a good life, kindly lived, always has its rewards.
reviews.author: Tom Bond

reviews.text: Pain and Glory is Almodóvar's most deeply affecting film to date that highlights Banderas' talent through a subtly emotive performance.
reviews.author: Katie Smith-Wong

reviews.text: Pain & Glory might see Almodóvar working in a minor key but it is a major work, graced with career-best work from Antonio Banderas.
reviews.author: Ian Freer

reviews.text: Pain & Glory is another victory for the auteur Pedro Almodovar and sees Antonio Banderas deliver a career-best performance as an ageing artist undergoing an existential crisis.
reviews.author: Lewis Knight

reviews.text: ......an honest and remorseful examination of a man who has had more regrets than delights - more pain than glory. An 8 1/2 style framework where Almodóvar can examine what if, and what is.
reviews.author: Anthony Frajman

reviews.text: The movie is of course visually sumptuous, but there's also a confident maturity in the storytelling that makes several moments drop-dead gorgeous. It's, quite simply, a stunner.
reviews.author: Rich Cline

reviews.text: "Pain and Glory" is a lovely, moving and compelling work, like every Almodovar picture.
reviews.author: Uri Klein

reviews.text: Pain and Glory is a personal movie about the dedication to make films and about first love. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Israel Acosta Aroche

reviews.text: A very complex character study; impeccably acted, written and directed. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Sebastian Zavala Kahn

reviews.text: Pain and Glory is one of the best films of Almodóvar, in which a deep emotional journey is made. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Lucero Calderón

reviews.text: We'll hardly find in contemporary cinema such a vigorous embodiment of physical pain and existential anxiety, as the one achieved by the character of Salvador Mallo. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Carlos Bonfil

reviews.text: A delightful performance on the part of Penelope Cruz. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: William Venegas

reviews.text: A new masterpiece in Almodóvar's filmography. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Juan Carlos Ugarelli

reviews.text: Pain and Glory is not only one of Almodovar's most self-referential films, it is also one of his best.
reviews.author: Harris Dang

reviews.text: The film is suggestive and hushed, kept in that encounter between dualities and contradictions, pains and glories that have been and will be Almodóvar's life. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Erick Estrada

reviews.text: Talking about the Almodóvar's movie Dolor y Gloria is talking about a contemplative and extremely human film. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Daniela Sagastegui Avilés

reviews.text: The film is an obligation and necessity for all those viewers who throughout the years have learned to know and love Almodóvar. [Full Review in Spanish
reviews.author: Luis Fernando Galván

reviews.text: Antonio Banderas gives one of the best performances of his career. [Full review in Portuguese.]
reviews.author: Pablo Villaça

reviews.text: The sophistication of his (Almodóvar) work has reached equally admirable levels of maturity, without going through any ostentation. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Leonardo Garcia Tsao

reviews.text: Banderas accomplishes an extremely difficult performance. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Javier Porta Fouz

reviews.text: A great film that when it ends, you're left with a desire to see more and more. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Fernando E. Juan Lima

reviews.text: Pain and Glory is a quiet, deeply emotional movie that illuminates how much the creative process can be a cathartic, therapeutic exercise in healing. It's a summation of sorts, a reconciliation, and a paean to filmmaking itself.
reviews.author: Stephen Garrett

reviews.text: ... an autumnal memory piece that arrives at a state of hard-won grace and serenity.
reviews.author: Dennis Lim

reviews.text: In the act of remembering and reconciling, the protagonist and the director show a vulnerability that goes beyond the homage and, although it does not stop idealizing, it envelops us and distracts us towards ourselves. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Alonso Díaz de la Vega

reviews.text: A rather distanced affair, albeit sprinkled with these small, beautiful moments of personal filmmaking
reviews.author: Jordan Ruimy

reviews.text: Almodóvar is optimistic that pain, whether mental or physical, can, once addressed, lead to genuine glory.
reviews.author: Manuela Lazic

reviews.text: While some of us may miss the subversive wackiness of his earlier films, the Spanish maestro shows that, like himself, his filmmaking has aged pretty well.
reviews.author: Kong Rithdee

reviews.text: Pain and Glory becomes a good movie when it shows that it is possible to find insight and that it can end up resuscitating the most recondite childhood. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Àngel Quintana

reviews.text: I can't think of another living director whose examination of the creative process could be so emotionally involving.
reviews.author: Alistair Ryder

reviews.text: Pain and Glory is less electric than Almódovar's earlier and more impassioned melodramas, but no less colourful.
reviews.author: Ella Kemp

reviews.text: Pain and Glory is Almodóvar's best work for years, marvellously framed and composed, comparatively restrained for him, hugely enjoyable moment by moment.
reviews.author: David Sexton

reviews.text: A film that [Almodovar's faithful followers] will surely enjoy. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Pablo O. Scholz

reviews.text: A glorious ode to the power of cinema and an absolute delight to watch.
reviews.author: Rebecca Harrison

reviews.text: Pain and Glory, the filmmaker's best and most personal movie in years, brings him back to mortal terrain.
reviews.author: Eric Kohn

reviews.text: Everything about Pain and Glory is awake and alive, and Almodóvar's nerve endings become ours, too.
reviews.author: Stephanie Zacharek

reviews.text: Banderas looks the part and does the best he can with the material provided.
reviews.author: Joseph Walsh

reviews.text: While hardly the director's most emotionally honest work, it's a story that speaks compellingly, if a touch reticently, about the patchwork nature of our lives.
reviews.author: Emma Simmonds

reviews.text: The hangdog expression is riven with pain, and [Banderas] plays Mallo as emotionally cauterised yet beneath it all still desperate to connect, to love and to make more films.
reviews.author: Kevin Maher

reviews.text: But unless you view Pain and Glory through a filter of deep affection for Almodóvar, you will see it as minor work: not painful, but not glorious, either.
reviews.author: Nicholas Barber

reviews.text: A film of solidity, precision and conviction unavoidable by a director in full artistic maturity. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Diego Batlle

reviews.text: There's plenty to admire, including the lead performance.
reviews.author: A.A. Dowd

reviews.text: However loosely "Pain and Glory" may play with the facts, it never feels less than truthful.
reviews.author: Justin Chang

reviews.text: Pedro Almodóvar's latest only occasionally captures the spry, comedic rhythms and impassioned intensity of his finest work.
reviews.author: Sam C. Mac

reviews.text: As well as expressing his views on love, loss and filmmaking, Almodóvar addresses broader political and social themes, offering thinly-veiled critiques of Catholicism and General Franco's authoritarian leadership.
reviews.author: Adam Woodward

reviews.text: Laced with autobiographical details, his new film is a beautiful, full-hearted celebration of the craft of filmmaking, as well as queer and maternal love.
reviews.author: Bradley Warren

reviews.text: The kind of indulgent and self-absorbed film that only a director with such a glittering career behind him would be allowed to get away with.
reviews.author: Geoffrey Macnab

reviews.text: There is something incomplete or unfinished in this work, but perhaps this simply represents the condition of life itself. Pain and Glory leaves you with a sweet sadness, but a sharp appetite for the next film.
reviews.author: Peter Bradshaw

reviews.text: A mature work of meticulously tuned meta-fiction...
reviews.author: Peter Debruge

reviews.text: The film often rings hollow.
reviews.author: Tim Robey

reviews.text: Pain and Glory may be too meandering to live up to the lofty standards of Almodóvar's best work, but for aficionados it is, if nothing else, a fascinating insight into how the great Spaniard may see himself.
reviews.author: Raphael Abraham

reviews.text: The effect is a patchwork rather than an interwoven whole; the wistfully self-reflexive tone will appeal to fans of the less emphatic, more meditative end of the Almodovar spectrum.
reviews.author: Wendy Ide

reviews.text: Pedro Almodóvar's heartrending, meditative, and deeply confessional culmination of his prolonged immersion in the waters of autofiction.
reviews.author: Manu Yáñez

reviews.text: Banderas produces a virtuouso performance, probably the best of his career. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Jordi Campeny

reviews.text: Almodóvar brings us back to his very distinctive world... with several self-referential and metalinguistic winks. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Ignacio Navarro

reviews.text: The film reaches a level of perfection that is difficult to surpass. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Luis Martínez

reviews.text: Indeed watching the film, which is more about pain than glory, sometimes feels a little too much like a couple of hours in the company of your ailing, aged aunt: You feel her pain, but you wish she wouldn't go on about it so much.
reviews.author: Jonathan Holland

reviews.text: My problem with Banderas's interpretation is that the character leaves me cold or smells of eternal imposture. Everyone has fun as they want or as they can. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Carlos Boyero

reviews.text: All this adds a film at once honest and exhibitionist, but perfectly consistent with the creative moment Almodóvar lives today. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: John Tones

reviews.text: One of Almodóvar's most exciting works. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Andrea G. Bermejo

synopsis: An aging Spanish film director in the middle of a creative crisis revisits memorable events of his past.
